static_traits.name: Ge Ping
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive husband and friends, but has not yet shared specific frustrations and failure feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior counseling or treatment experience

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling overwhelmed and frustrated when learning a new violin piece, struggling to master it after repeated practice, producing 'just give up' thoughts.
basic_info.core_demands: This sense of frustration weakens overall drive and confidence, affecting musical skill and daily life, so hoping to reduce failure and giving-up thoughts through counseling, restoring drive and confidence.
growth_experiences: Went through a very difficult phase during nursing school, but persisted and received support from classmates and family, finally graduating smoothly, gaining significant achievement and self-efficacy.

core_beliefs: Needing others' help equals my incompetence

special_situations.event: Every time she practices this new violin piece, she repeatedly gets stuck and finds it hard to make progress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still cannot learn this piece in a few weeks, it means I will never learn it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles practice and searches online tutorials, but after continued frustration begins to consider giving up
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This will simply never happen; I should just give up

special_situations.event: When thinking of seeking extra help from the violin teacher or husband
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I need others' help, it means I am incompetent, even troubling the other person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Insists on solving problems alone and avoids help-seeking to maintain an 'independent and competent' image
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should handle it myself, cannot trouble others

special_situations.event: Comparing one's own practice performance with the high expectation of 'excelling at the violin'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only reaching an excellent level counts as success; otherwise it is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting excessively high goals, negating current efforts and any small progress

special_situations.event: Still no obvious improvement after trying different practice techniques and online tutorials
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: This failure means future failures too
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Inferring overall ability from several setbacks, gradually developing a tendency to give up
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never learn this piece

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as competent and excellent in learning and performance, while obtaining support and understanding when needed
core_conflict.fear: Fearing appearing incompetent or becoming others' burden, thus being judged as complaining or incapable
defense_goal: Maintains self-esteem by insisting on solving independently and avoiding help-seeking, avoiding disappointing others or burdening them

object_relations.self_representation: Someone needing to solve problems independently, unable to trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: Others as people who may be burdened by me or judge insufficiency

object_relations.self_representation: A learner who hesitates in difficulty and needs help but finds it hard to speak up
object_relations.object_representation: Teachers/family as potential supporters, and also others who may reveal one's 'incompetence'

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to seek help from her husband or teacher, or to speak up and express vulnerable needs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting seeking help as troubling others, also meaning one's incompetence (transference: imposing the inner 'cannot trouble others' rule onto relationships)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'I do not want to trouble others' in a gentle but firm tone, prioritizing alternatives not involving help-seeking, reducing emotional self-disclosure.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When counseling focuses on feelings of frustration and invites deeper emotional experience
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Views deep expression as complaining or losing control, turning instead to plan and technique discussion to keep a sense of control
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using analytic, task-oriented language, discussing practice strategies and steps, weakening subjective emotional vocabulary, maintaining a calm, restrained tone.

manifestations: Developing 'more practice is meaningless anyway' thoughts when repeatedly frustrated practicing violin pieces
Inferring current difficulty as unchangeable, thus doubting the value of continued effort
outcomes: Relationship tension with spouse and children

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should handle it myself' phrasing
Treating 'solving problems independently, not troubling others' as an unshakable self-standard

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Knowing the teachers and family can provide support, still restrains the impulse to seek help, and instead bears setbacks alone
Stopping actions of expressing needs on the grounds of 'I should not trouble others'

exception_events.target_problem: When practicing difficult violin pieces, the client usually feels strong frustration and has thoughts of giving up.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During the difficult nursing-school phase, the client did not choose to give up like now, but persisted and sought classmates' and family's support, finally graduating smoothly with a sense of achievement.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different support and approach — received peer and family support then, and adopted persistence and cooperation strategies, so a deviation from 'giving up' appeared in the high-difficulty learning task.

positive_force: Once achieved success in a difficult study task through persistence and help-seeking (the experience of graduating from nursing school)
Tendency to actively try different practice methods and online resources
Has a supportive spouse and friends network
negative_force: Cognitive patterns such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and predicting failure are strong
Viewing seeking help as incompetence or troubling others, thus avoiding support
Drive and decreased confidence, low mood affecting sleep and work, interpersonal relationships

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing and a tendency to give up arise when practicing difficult violin pieces, and seeking help from others is avoided
antecedent: Starting to practice this new piece
Repeatedly gets stuck during practice; progress is slow
Thinking about situations of seeking help from teachers or family
target_behavior.core_reason: High standard expectations for performance trigger black-and-white and failure-predicting cognition; linking seeking help with 'incompetence, troubling others', leading to Self-denial and avoiding support.
target_behavior.function: Short-term evasion of the pain of failure and frustration, maintains the self-image of 'independence and competence'.
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, sleep affected, decline in work performance, strained relationships with family members, practice stagnating and reinforcing giving-up thoughts.
